column2: which piano the recordings are: the University of Iowa MIS notes the page grades (Piano.pp.A3, Piano.mf.A3, Piano.ff.A3, Piano.mf.C6) are a Steinway Model B (apps/instrument-lab/README.md), while the render is a reconstructed Model D (Boutillon, Ege and Paulello 2012 Fig. 2 with estimated fields, steinway_d.rs header); how one partial of one key decays follows the board's driving-point conductance at that frequency (computed for this board at C6 in u-board-damping), and the recorded board's is unknown
column4: any same-instrument claim, and the grader's per-key decay_db_s, partial_traj_db and env_db for one note
column5: Model B board geometry and bridge data, or recordings of a Model D

column2: the unison detuning, detune_cents 0.8 per member (the three members of a course at -0.8, 0 and +0.8 cents), is a literal in the scale builders (steinway_scale.rs, whose header lists unison counts, duplex lengths and patch areas as estimated and names no source for a detune, and geometry.rs, under the comment that its nominal constants are not specimen measurements); no measured distribution of unison detuning in a tuned concert grand was found in open sources (searched 2026-10-30: the sources found describe the mechanism of the double decay, not a distribution)
column3: unbounded; at 0.8 cents the members of C6 (1050.5 Hz) are 0.49 Hz apart, and three equal members first cancel at 1/(3 x 0.49 Hz) = 0.68 s, near the minimum of that render's C6 fundamental (0.9 s in the bridge velocity, 100 ms windows)
column4: the time and depth of beating dips; the level of the aftersound (in a render of the graded recipe without the air load, the C6 fundamental is 27 to 34 dB under its peak from 0.4 to 0.7 s, the recording 10 to 23 dB, pressure envelopes in 100 ms windows); the second stage of the double decay
column5: a measured unison-detune distribution for a tuned grand, or an owner measurement

column2: the graded board's modal damping is the authored damping,0.015 (steinway_d.rs, zeta of every mode, loss factor about 0.03); steinway_d.rs documents that the cited wood-loss boards (Qiu 2026 and Ono 1996 rows, pexfp.373) are opt-in through build_with_material_loss, and piano_geometry has no flag to select them; per mail 9339 the material-loss board is held for an owner ruling (pexfp.373 unit D, mail 6477)
column3: Boutillon and Ege 2013 (J. Sound Vib. 332:4261, arXiv 1305.3057 p. 5) state that the loss factor is about 2 % +- 1 % over several kHz and the modal density about 0.06 modes per Hz below 1.1 kHz, from an upright in playing condition; this board's dump (--dump-board, 1600 Hz band, 82 modes) has 0.064 modes per Hz over 700 to 1400 Hz
column4: board ring-down; whether the air load counts radiation twice on a damping of unstated origin (RAYLEIGH_LOADING.md: damping identified from total measured decay may already include radiation); per-key prompt decay: from those dumped modes the board's driving-point conductance at C6's 1050.5 Hz is 8.7e-4 m/(N s), 2.0 times its mean over +-20 % (4.4e-4)
column5: the owner ruling on pexfp.373 unit D, and the source of the 0.015

column2: the string's inclination to the board plane at the speaking termination (downbearing) and the bridge-pin height above the panel midplane, per key: the graded board file carries a triangle and barycentric station per bridge row and a beam section (area, bending inertia, eccentricity) for the bridge, built from literals in steinway_d.rs (a flat plate with downbearing outside its image; bridge widths named as explicit estimates in its header; a section 26 mm wide and 44 to 22 mm high with no source stated beside it); Boutillon, Ege and Paulello 2012 (arXiv 1210.3948, all six pages read) gives neither; the former authored BRIDGE_AXIAL_PROJECTION = 0.06 of longitudinal_string.rs (its comment: about 1.8 degrees of downbearing plus a 28 mm bridge-cap lever arm, no source recorded) no longer exists in grand_piano: the axial participation row of a waves key is derived from the board, with the arm taken as the outer fibre of the string-side beam that holds the station, e + h/2 with h = sqrt(12 I / A) from that beam's row (a rectangular section and a string riding on the outer fibre are assumed: 36.5 mm at A3, 28.5 mm at C6) and sin(downbearing) = 0 because the plate is flat; the same 0.06 remains, labelled, in piano_exterior (EXTERIOR_AXIAL_RATIO) and in the live engine (engine-piano stretch.rs, LIVE_BRIDGE_AXIAL_RATIO)
column3: unbounded for both inputs; the derived rocking term is proportional to the arm, so an arm 20 % larger or smaller scales it by 20 %; a downbearing of 1.8 degrees (the figure the removed comment named, no source recorded) would add sin(1.8 degrees) = 0.031 times the vertical row to the axial row, about 5 % of the A3 coupling ratio in u-string-direction; the row is read only for keys with a waves row (A3 in the graded set)
column4: the size of the axial drive of the bridge by longitudinal waves (phantom partials at the axial modes, 3273 Hz and its multiples for A3), and the second transverse polarization (STRING_POLARIZATION.md: no measured Model D bridge heights, axes or lateral drag are inferred; the frame file needs an arm vector, string axis and lateral damper ratio per key)
column5: per-key downbearing angle and bridge-pin height above the panel midplane for a Model D or B (Conklin 1996, J. Acoust. Soc. Am. 100:695, not reached), or an owner measurement; and a lateral bridge mobility, which no open source found gives

column2: the string's direction in the board plane at its bridge contact: the board file carries no string endpoint (agraffe, capo bar, hitch pin) and no bearing points; the derived axial row takes it perpendicular to the bridge in plan, with the speaking length toward decreasing y (the RT-0425 frame's front edge, from which its published contacts run straight back); that is an assumption, and the x axis, y axis and front edge are the preset's frame, not a property of a board file
column3: A3 on the graded board's 82-mode 1600 Hz source slice: the coupling ratio R (square root of the near-partial-weighted sum of squares of the axial row over that of the vertical row; modes within two half-widths of an A3 partial) is 0.61 for the assumed direction, 0.37 to 0.63 over every direction in the plane and 0.50 to 0.63 within 30 degrees of it, so every A3 value is 6 to 10 times the former authored 0.06; C6: 0.33 assumed, 0.12 to 0.36 over every direction, 0.23 to 0.36 within 30 degrees
column4: the size of every axial participation row and its sign (the sign of the row follows the sign of the axis, so it sets the phase of the axial drive against the transverse strain)
column5: per-key string endpoints or bearing support points for a Model D or B (the points bearing_geometry.rs takes as front and rear supports), or an owner measurement
